Table 12: Comparison of insights across domains and methods. Method 1 is our pipeline, Method 2 uses direct GPT-4o prompting, and Method 3 combines FAISS-based retrieval with GPT-4o. Our pipeline consistently generates novel and actionable insights, while other methods tend to rephrase content. For Methods 2 and 3, we show the variant (with or without chain-of-thought prompts) that achieves the higher score for a clearer comparison.
Table 2: Set-level scores across models and themes on research paper collections (SCOpE-QA). Best results are shown in green and second-best in red. Insight-level scores are reported in Table 10.

Figure 6: Thematic clusters from the Graph ML collection. Each node corresponds to a document segment, and edges represent semantic relationships. Clustering highlights distinct research themes within the Graph ML domain.
Figure 7: Clusters within the RL collection. Nodes represent semantically grouped document segments, showing recurring research topics and methodological patterns.

Table 5: Summary statistics of the document collection across domains. The table reports the number of files, average file length in tokens and words, and the average length of questions and answers in both words and tokens.

Table 6: Ablation on the number of clusters used by KMeans. The hyperparameter num_cluster controls how many clusters are formed over the chunk set. Results are reported on six research themes selected from INSIGHTGEN. Setting the number of clusters to √ n gives the best and most consistent performance and is used in the final system.
Figure 2: SCOpE-QA dataset curation pipeline overview, highlighting collection curation and QA generation.
Table 11: Insight-level scores across models and domainson internal document collections (non-scientific domain). Best results are highlighted in green, with second-best results in red.

Figure 8: Clusters in the Quantization collection. Nodes correspond to document segments, and edges indicate semantic relationships. Clustering highlights both technical and application-specific topics within quantization research.

Table 3: Set-level scores across models and domains on internal non-scientific document collections. Best results are shown in green and second-best in red. Insight-level scores are reported in Table 11.
Table 10: Insight-level scores are reported across models and themes on research paper collections. Best results are highlighted in green, with second-best results in red.
Figure 4: Example insights showing differences in type and content. These insights provide additional observations and reflections from a set of documents on analyzing mental health on Twitter.
Figure 5: Example insights showing differences in type and content. These insights provide additional observations and reflections from a set of documents on analyzing mental health on Twitter.

Table 1: Summary statistics of the document collection across research themes. The table reports the number of files, average file length in tokens and words, and the average length of questions and answers in both words and tokens.
